detail.text: That connection holds.Your answer: Accept: one fully consuming accepting path is enough.Correct answer: Accept: one fully consuming accepting path is enough.Nondeterministic acceptance is existential: at least one possible path must consume the whole word and finish in an accepting state. Other paths may fail, stop early or end elsewhere. There is no vote or probability in this model.Try this transfer: Explain why counting the accepting paths is unnecessary for this accept/reject decision, and why a path that leaves input unread is insufficient.Follow the next thread →

The set is {q0,q1,q2}. Repeating a cycle does not create new states.Try this transfer: Why can a visited-state traversal stop even though there are infinitely many walks around the q0–q1 cycle?Follow the next thread →

Here’s the correction.Your answer: The single state q0.Correct answer: The subset {q0,q1,q2}.The DFA represents every possible NFA state after each consumed prefix, including the empty prefix. Its start subset must therefore include q0 and all states epsilon-reachable from q0: {q0,q1,q2}.Try this transfer: If only q2 is accepting, does this start subset accept the empty word? Explain without consuming a symbol.Follow the next thread →

Other, nonaccepting members do not undo the successful possibility.Try this transfer: Give one accepting and one rejecting subset for the same NFA accepting set. Explain why the number of rejecting members is irrelevant.Follow the next thread →

Closing the resulting empty union again gives the empty set. Thus both transitions return to it, making it a valid rejecting sink whenever it is reachable.Try this transfer: Is ∅ necessarily reachable in every subset construction? Distinguish the full power set from the subsets reached from the start.Follow the next thread →

What is the next active set, and can later input revive it without any active state?Follow the next thread →
